messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: setCdf and caching
parts:
Hi,

I was just wondering, if I am frequently changing the cdf for a
AffymetrixCelSet am I going to run into any problems with something that
has been cached? Is it better to make duplicate objects with their own
cdf? setCdf(cs,cdf) actually takes a bit of time, so it's probably
better for that reason.

Similarly, if I call setCdf(cs,cdf) within a function, is that a bad
idea in terms of what it will do to the user? Should I make the user
give me two cs objects (and then check that they actually access the
same data)?

I am trying to write some functions that will bridge certain gaps
between an analysis done on a cdf that overlaps another cdf in terms of
what probes are included in each (but differ in what groups/units probes
are assigned to as well as having probes in one that aren't in the
other) and I'm suddenly wondering what I might be doing!

Best,
Elizabeth

parts:
On Feb 12, 2008 1:19 PM, Elizabeth Purdom <epu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> I was just wondering, if I am frequently changing the cdf for a
> AffymetrixCelSet am I going to run into any problems with something that
> has been cached? Is it better to make duplicate objects with their own
> cdf? setCdf(cs,cdf) actually takes a bit of time, so it's probably
> better for that reason.

There are two types of caching: i) in memory cache and ii) in file
cache. The code should be careful enough to detect if you change CDF;
the getChipType(..., fullname=TRUE) is used as one of the object used
to generate the unique cache key. I'm quite sure I went through and
checked this. Also, when you call setCdf() on the set and in turn
each file (that's why it takes time), clearCache() in each object
should be called. That in turn is responsible to clear all in-memory
cached results.

>
> Similarly, if I call setCdf(cs,cdf) within a function, is that a bad
> idea in terms of what it will do to the user? Should I make the user
> give me two cs objects (and then check that they actually access the
> same data)?

This definitely sounds like a potential trap for bugs and mistakes.
So some effort in protecting against such errors is needed.

>
> I am trying to write some functions that will bridge certain gaps
> between an analysis done on a cdf that overlaps another cdf in terms of
> what probes are included in each (but differ in what groups/units probes
> are assigned to as well as having probes in one that aren't in the
> other) and I'm suddenly wondering what I might be doing!

Is this something done orthogonal to actual data? You basically
compare two CDFs? If you could write the function to take two CDF
objects, that should be safer (and maybe clearer?). For instance, we
already have:

identical(x,y) for all R objects
all.equal(target, current) for all R objects
equals(this, other) for all R.oo Object:s
compare(this, other) for comparing two AffymetrixCdfFile:s

Hope this helps

Henrik

> Best,
> Elizabeth

On Feb 12, 2008 2:55 PM, Elizabeth Purdom <epu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>
> Hi Henrik,
> I have a question about what you sent.
>
> >> Similarly, if I call setCdf(cs,cdf) within a function, is that a bad
> >> idea in terms of what it will do to the user? Should I make the user
> >> give me two cs objects (and then check that they actually access the
> >> same data)?
> >>
> >
> > This definitely sounds like a potential trap for bugs and mistakes.
> > So some effort in protecting against such errors is needed.
> >
> >
> Sorry, I'm not sure what you mean by this -- that either one is a bad
> idea? Or just the second idea? If I set the cdf within the function,
> will this change the cdf in the global environment? (Normally that's not
> what happens to changes within R functions)

No, it won't change anything in the *global environment*, but if you
have a AffymetrixCelSet 'cs' and call a function that does setCdf() on
that object, the new CDF *will* remain after returning (*or being
interrupted*). Thus, a method with the side effect of changing the
CDF might be confusing. If you use setCdf() in a method, I recommend
that you use:

foo <- function(this, ...) {
oldCdf <- getCdf(this);
on.exit({
if (!identical(oldCdf, getCdf(this))) {
setCdf(this, oldCdf);
}
})

newCdf <- ...
setCdf(this, newCdf);
...
}

The above will "guarantee" that your method returns having the old CDF
set regardless if the methods normally or by an error. Note, there
will always be the risk that the user press Ctrl+C while resetting the
CDF via the last setCdf(). Then the reset will not be complete. I
guess that could be controlled for that further by using a
tryCatch(setCdf(this, oldCdf), interrupt=function(intr) {
throw("Failed to reset CDF before returning due to a requested
interrupt.")}).

>
> Unfortunately, what I want to do is not orthogonal to the data. It's
> taking the results from a plm (e.g. chip effects) and applying them, in
> a certain sense, to additional data not used in the plm fitting. The
> additional data comes from the other cdf file, which indexes different
> probes.

So, you can uniquely infer the 2nd CDF from the 1st?

/Henrik
